thread:
support-john: AcmePay reporting sudden jump in latency and unexpected US region traffic. They think they were pinned to eu-west but ~25-35% of requests show X-Redwood-Region: us-east and p95 latency increased 30ms->210ms. Can someone pick this up?
maria-cs: are they on Hosted or Dedicated? any recent policy changes from their Console?
support-john: Hosted. Customer edited failover policy last week — said they just reordered primary/secondary. Start time ~2024-11-05T09:10Z. Repro from our EU node below.
support-john: ```bash
# quick repro from eu node
curl -v -H "X-Client-Region: eu-west" -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions
# observed response headers:
# X-Redwood-Region: us-east-1
# x-request-latency-ms: 214
```
support-john: body/auth all normal, but routing wrong. They attached the policy export (redacted):
support-john: ```json
{
  "id": "P-ACME-2024",
  "failover": {
    "sticky": true,
    "sticky_ttl_ms": 60000,
    "targets": [
      {"region": "eu-west-1", "weight": 0.0},
      {"region": "us-east-1", "weight": 1.0},
      {"region": "eu-west-1", "weight": 100.0}
    ]
  }
}
```

devin-eng: that targets array is a red flag. eu-west appears twice; weight 0.0 then later 100.0. Router eval uses explicit priority when present, otherwise falls back to array order. We recently had a normalization change: weights <1.0 get truncated to 0 which effectively disables that entry.
sre-liz: +1. The recent router release also changed how small decimal weights are handled. Any weight <1 becomes 0 after normalization. If the duplicate entry ended up earlier in the array with 0 weight, router will skip it and pick the next matching target (us-east in this case). Also note: sticky behavior had a change where sticky_ttl_ms < 30000 was considered transient by the session cache; sticky_ttl_ms=60000 should be fine but the incorrect early target selection set sticky to us-east.
ops-anna: concrete triage steps: (1) run admin debug for that API key to see effective policy; (2) repro with X-Route-Trace to get decision trace; (3) review Console change history for that policy id and the client-side save payload.
support-john: we grabbed an admin debug for a repro call. X-Route-Trace header returned: 

X-Route-Trace: eval_start -> targets[0] region=eu-west-1 weight=0 -> skipped -> targets[1] region=us-east-1 weight=1 -> selected -> sticky_set=us-east-1 ttl=60s

support-john: so router skipped the first eu-west entry (weight 0) and selected us-east which then got sticky. Customer insists Console showed eu-west first when they saved. Could be a save serialization bug.
devin-eng: hypotheses: (A) Console client serialized two entries by mistake when user attempted to move canary entry; (B) server-side merge/dedupe logic reordered/merged entries in an unintended way; (C) weight normalization bug turned a tiny canary weight into 0. Repro plan: reproduce in staging by saving a policy with duplicate regions and mixed decimal weights to observe server-side canonicalization.
sre-liz: mitigation we pushed: we updated the customer's policy to remove duplicates and set explicit integer priorities so ordering is unambiguous. Example patched policy we applied: 

patched policy snippet: 
{
  "failover": {
    "targets": [
      {"region": "eu-west-1", "priority": 0, "weight": 100},
      {"region": "us-east-1", "priority": 1, "weight": 0}
    ],
    "sticky": true,
    "sticky_ttl_ms": 60000
  }
}

sre-liz: After applying change we cleared the route cache for that policy id and asked the customer to retry. infra-bot shows the config update as a canary roll: 

infra-bot: route-config-updater: policy P-ACME-2024 updated by devin-eng at 2024-11-06T11:40:02Z (canary=10%)

devin-eng: canary at 10% then rolled to 100% after positive checks. @sre-liz can you confirm traces from EU clients?
sre-liz: confirmed — first 120 samples post-patch from their key show X-Redwood-Region: eu-west-1 and p95 latency back to ~30-50ms. Repro looks fixed.
billing-tom: note: customer incurred ~$95 cross-region egress costs during window. CS may request credit once root cause is confirmed.
maria-cs: I'll file a credit request and include start/end timestamps once SRE confirms final timeline.

support-john: root cause summary: malformed failover targets (duplicate region entries + decimal weight that normalized to 0) combined with array-order precedence caused us-east to be selected and sticky set incorrectly. Immediate fix: dedupe regions and use explicit integer priorities + clear route cache. Longer-term fixes: server-side validation to reject duplicate region entries, warn on decimal weights <1.0, and Console preview of normalized policy before save.
ops-anna: added follow-up tasks to product backlog: Console warning for duplicate regions, server-side save validation, and a guardrail for tiny weights.
support-john: customer reports all traffic now hitting eu-west and latencies normalized. CS will follow up on credits. Closing the ticket after confirmations. Thanks team. :white_check_mark:
